steps.title: The major scale recipe
steps.body:
**major scale** means a seven-note scale built with this **scale formula**: whole, whole, half, whole, whole, whole, half. A scale formula is the list of gaps between neighbouring notes. On one string, whole means two frets and half means one.

**Why it matters:** The same recipe works from any starting note; you can check the gaps instead of memorising every fret.

steps.title: Find the notes
steps.body: C to D and D to E are whole steps. E to F is a half step. Continue F to G, G to A and A to B with whole steps; B to C is a half step.

items.prompt: Play C, D, E, F, G, A, B, C in that order, one note at a time.

steps.title: Make it familiar
steps.body: On string 5, try frets 3, 5, 7, 8, 10, 12, 14, 15. It is the same C major scale as the shorter route across strings. Stop if the reach feels awkward.
